clue.text: Property man producing photographs

definitions.meaning: a businessperson who buys land and builds houses or offices on it
the chemical bath that brings out the image on exposed film

explanation.surface: An estate agent type who also happens to take pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the builder who turns land into housing estates; the other is the darkroom chemical that makes a latent image visible on film.

clue.text: One's about to perform outside for a music party

indicators.note: the words for perform go round the outside of the other pieces

parts.note: to perform is to do
one is I, so one's is I'S
C, short for circa, means about

explanation.surface: Someone is about to play an outdoor set at a party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One's' is read as 'one is', giving I + S; 'about' is C (circa). Both go inside DO, signalled by 'outside'.
explanation.definitionFit: A party where people dance to recorded pop music under flashing lights.

clue.text: I turn green first, then get dizziness

indicators.note: the clue tells us the word for green comes first, ahead of the I

parts.note: vert is the heraldic term for green
a go is a turn, as in 'your go'

explanation.surface: Someone feels nauseous and then goes giddy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'I turn green' reads as feeling sick, but 'first' just says the colour, in its heraldic form, goes before the I.
explanation.definitionFit: The condition of feeling the world spin, especially when looking down from a height.

clue.text: Kafkaesque novels set in places where affairs are conducted

indicators.note: Kafka's writing is nightmarishly distorted, so these letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: Kafka's novels take place in locations where romantic intrigues happen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Kafkaesque' is the anagram signal: the letters of NOVELS SET are rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Secret hideaways where illicit lovers meet are known by this romantic name.

clue.text: Patient line misinterpreted, like some of the psalms

indicators.note: something misinterpreted is read wrongly, so the letters are reordered

explanation.surface: A patient misreads a line from the Psalms.
explanation.walkthrough: 'misinterpreted' signals an anagram of PATIENT LINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Seven psalms are traditionally called the penitential psalms because they express sorrow for sin.

clue.text: Spoil is mounting — pack tight

indicators.note: in a down clue, mounting means the word climbs upward, read from the bottom

parts.note: to mar is to spoil

explanation.surface: Ruin is rising, so cram everything in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'mounting' means reading upwards: MAR (spoil) turned round.
explanation.definitionFit: To force something down hard, as when cramming earth into a hole.

clue.text: Left before the recess in error

indicators.note: the letter for left is placed ahead of the next piece

parts.note: an apse is a vaulted recess in a church

explanation.surface: Someone made a slip just before the alcove.
explanation.walkthrough: An APSE is the semicircular recess at the end of a church.
explanation.definitionFit: A slip or momentary failure, as in a lapse of memory.

clue.text: Moderate obstacle when riding

parts.note: a let is an obstruction, as in 'without let or hindrance' and in tennis
a jockey who is riding a horse is said to be up

explanation.surface: A small obstacle met while out on horseback.
explanation.walkthrough: LET is an old word for hindrance; a jockey riding is 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: To ease off or slacken, as rain does when it stops pouring.

clue.text: Social climber's name appears in fashionable rave-up

definitions.note: the 's stands for 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay

indicators.note: the letter for name sits inside the rearranged party word
to fashion is to shape, so rave-up is reshaped

explanation.surface: A snob's name is mentioned at a trendy party.
explanation.walkthrough: 'fashionable' is read as 'able to be fashioned', an anagram signal: RAVEUP becomes PARVEU, and 'appears in' puts N inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: An upstart who has risen suddenly to wealth or rank without the manners to match.

clue.text: Cockney says 'e's a gentleman

parts.note: a Londoner dropping his aitches describes a local man from his own part of the city

explanation.surface: A Londoner vouches for someone's good manners.
explanation.walkthrough: A Cockney is born within sound of Bow Bells in east London; the dropped H in 'e's is the giveaway of local speech.
explanation.definitionFit: A Cockney is a native of the eastern part of London, so such a man is a local of that area.

clue.text: Rent is on the way, having had a struggle

indicators.note: the word for torn comes after the street, as if sitting on it

parts.note: ST, short for street, is a way
rent here is the past participle of rend, meaning torn, like riven

explanation.surface: Someone has fought hard while the rent is due.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rent' looks like money paid to a landlord, but it is the past of rend: RIVEN, torn. It goes 'on' ST (street, a way).
explanation.definitionFit: The past participle of strive, to make great efforts or fight.

clue.text: The oldest city in China's ages

indicators.note: the ancient city is placed inside the word for pals

parts.note: in Cockney rhyming slang china plate means mate, so china's gives mates
Ur, in ancient Mesopotamia, is among the oldest known cities

explanation.surface: A remark about the age of China's most ancient city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'China' is not the country: in Cockney rhyming slang 'china plate' means mate.
explanation.definitionFit: To grow older or ripen, as wine or cheese does over time.

clue.text: Vegetable needs a little macaroni on it

indicators.note: only a small portion of the words macaroni on it is used, a run of letters inside them

explanation.surface: A recipe note says the pasta needs some vegetable on top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a little' tells us to take a short run of letters from inside MACARONI ON IT.
explanation.definitionFit: A bulb vegetable with layered rings that makes eyes water when cut.

clue.text: Viva voce for the aspiring singer?

definitions.text: Viva voce for the aspiring singer?

parts.words: Viva voce for the aspiring singer?
parts.note: an oral exam for a would-be vocalist would be a set song performed in front of examiners

explanation.surface: An oral examination for a would-be vocalist.
explanation.walkthrough: A viva voce is an oral exam; for a singer the 'oral exam' is literally a performance of a set piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A set composition that every competitor or examinee must perform, to compare their skill.

clue.text: Alternate directors for communications centre

parts.note: to alternate between two things is to switch
a company's directors form its board

explanation.surface: Directors take turns running the telephone exchange.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Alternate' is a verb here, giving SWITCH; the directors are the BOARD.
explanation.definitionFit: The panel where telephone calls are connected by an operator in an office or exchange.

clue.text: Bovine girl embracing black African

indicators.note: the mythical girl's name wraps around the letter for black

parts.note: Io, in Greek myth, was turned into a heifer by Zeus
B is the abbreviation for black, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A cow-like young woman hugging a dark-skinned man.
explanation.walkthrough: IO is the girl of Greek myth turned into a heifer; she goes round B for black.
explanation.definitionFit: A member of a people of south-eastern Nigeria, now usually spelt Igbo.

clue.text: Make unwilling Pluto sit below at home

indicators.note: in a down entry, the pieces for Pluto and sit come under the word for at home

parts.note: someone who is in is at home
Dis is another name for Pluto, Roman god of the underworld
to sit for a portrait is to pose

explanation.surface: Telling a planet to sit beneath the house would put anyone off.
explanation.walkthrough: Pluto is not the planet or the cartoon dog but the underworld god, also called DIS. DIS + POSE go 'below' IN in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: To render someone disinclined or reluctant to do something.

clue.text: Money set aside for a very rainy day?

definitions.text: Money set aside for a very rainy day?

parts.words: Money set aside for a very rainy day?
parts.note: savings put by for a downpour so heavy that everything goes under water

explanation.surface: Savings kept for an emergency.
explanation.walkthrough: Saving 'for a rainy day' means for hard times; a very rainy day would leave you submerged. The phrase is really a fund set aside regularly to repay a debt.
explanation.definitionFit: A reserve built up by regular payments to pay off a debt or replace an asset.

clue.text: Large pet has to eat in the garden perhaps

indicators.note: the letters could perhaps be arranged otherwise, so they are reordered

explanation.surface: A big animal has to dine out in the garden.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' signals an anagram of EAT with GARDEN; 'in' simply tells us the two sets of letters are combined.
explanation.definitionFit: A huge breed of dog, among the tallest kept in homes.

clue.text: Lower deck accommodation for HMS Pinafore, perhaps?

definitions.text: Lower deck accommodation for HMS Pinafore, perhaps?

parts.words: Lower deck accommodation for HMS Pinafore, perhaps?
parts.note: not sailors' quarters on a warship but seating on a lower tier of a theatre staging a Gilbert and Sullivan operetta

explanation.surface: Where the ordinary sailors sleep aboard a navy ship.
explanation.walkthrough: HMS Pinafore is a Gilbert and Sullivan comic opera, not a real ship, so the 'lower deck' is a tier of seats in a theatre.
explanation.definitionFit: The first balcony in a theatre, once where evening dress was expected.

clue.text: Girl accepts a hint and takes refuge

definitions.note: the clue gives a verb phrase where the answer is a noun, meaning one who takes refuge

indicators.note: the girl's name takes the other letters inside it

parts.note: Eve is a girl's name
a cue is a hint or prompt

explanation.surface: A young woman takes a tip and shelters somewhere safe.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is loose: the answer is a person who takes refuge, not the act itself.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone moved away from danger, such as a child sent to the countryside in wartime.

clue.text: Baronet's father not English

indicators.note: not tells us the letter for English is left out of the word for father

parts.note: a sire is a male parent, especially of a horse

explanation.surface: A titled man's dad is not from England.
explanation.walkthrough: SIRE is a father; drop E for English.
explanation.definitionFit: A baronet's title, placed before his first name, is the same honorific a knight uses.

clue.text: Examine boy upset by malicious talk

parts.note: to scan is to examine closely

indicators.note: in a down entry, upset means turned upside down, so the word for boy reads upwards

parts.note: a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy is hurt by gossip after being looked over.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down entry 'upset' means turned upside down, so the boy is read upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Gossip that damages someone's reputation, or the outrage it causes.

clue.text: Are its accounts kept on tablets of stone?

definitions.text: Are its accounts kept on tablets of stone?

parts.words: Are its accounts kept on tablets of stone?
parts.note: a savings society named for the stone writing boards once used in schools, as if its ledgers were literally written on them

explanation.surface: Asking whether some organisation keeps records carved in rock.
explanation.walkthrough: A slate is a tablet of stone for writing on. The real thing is a British savings club whose members pay in a little weekly, often towards Christmas.
explanation.definitionFit: A mutual savings group into which members pay small weekly sums, shared out at year's end.

clue.text: See about note to girl

indicators.note: the name of the cathedral city goes around the musical note

parts.note: Ely is a cathedral city and bishop's see in Cambridgeshire
mi is the third note of the sol-fa scale

explanation.surface: Look around for a note to a young woman.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' is not 'look' but a bishop's diocese: ELY, a cathedral city in eastern England. It goes about MI, a note of the scale.
explanation.definitionFit: A common female first name.

clue.text: Toils in the bunkers

definitions.meaning: toils are nets or snares in which hunted animals are caught

explanation.surface: Working hard down in the sand pits.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Toils' looks like a verb for hard work, but it is the noun meaning snares, as in 'caught in the toils'.
explanation.definitionFit: Snares that catch animals; in golf, especially American usage, sand-filled hollows are called by the same word.

clue.text: Overcrowded city is rising in strength

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the letters read upwards, reversing them

parts.note: the Great Wen was William Cobbett's name for congested London

explanation.surface: A packed city is growing more powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: London was called 'the Great Wen' (a swollen growth) by Cobbett, so WEN is an overcrowded city. WEN + IS read upwards gives the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A tendon, and by extension muscular power or force.

clue.text: Medical man using round copper file

parts.note: O is round in shape
Cu is the chemical symbol for copper
a file can be a list or roll

explanation.surface: A doctor uses a circular metal file.
explanation.walkthrough: 'copper' is not a police officer but the metal, symbol CU.
explanation.definitionFit: An old word for an eye doctor or optician.

clue.text: It identifies a staff officer in a minor flap

definitions.meaning: the coloured collar patch worn by senior British army staff officers
a small tag or strip attached to something to pull it by

explanation.surface: A small panic about who is a staff officer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'flap' looks like a panic, but it is a small attached strip.
explanation.definitionFit: Red collar patches mark British staff officers, and the same word means a small projecting strip.

clue.text: Letting oneself go in desert

definitions.meaning: uninhibited freedom, as in dancing with wild enthusiasm
to desert is to walk out on and leave behind

explanation.surface: Losing self-control while out in an arid wilderness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'desert' is a verb, not the sandy place.
explanation.definitionFit: As a noun, carefree lack of restraint; as a verb, to forsake someone or something.

clue.text: Born in the East? Gosh, an armed opponent!

parts.note: E is the abbreviation for east
né, as in a man's birth name, means born
my! is an exclamation of surprise, like gosh

explanation.surface: Someone born in Asia turns out to be a hostile soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the East' is read as 'coming in after the East'; né is the French for born, as in a man's former name.
explanation.definitionFit: A foe or hostile force, especially one in war.

clue.text: A gardener possibly unexpected at a difficult time?

definitions.text: A gardener possibly unexpected at a difficult time?

parts.words: A gardener possibly unexpected at a difficult time?
parts.note: someone who works among flower beds, and the proverb that adversity makes strange companions

explanation.surface: A gardener showing up unexpectedly at an awkward moment.
explanation.walkthrough: A gardener tends beds, so is a 'bed fellow'; the saying 'adversity makes strange bedfellows' supplies the unexpected partner in hard times.
explanation.definitionFit: A close associate or partner, literally someone sharing a bed.
